messages.author: 81f2ee716ca4282f
messages.subject: How to provide matrix of integers to user-defined function
parts:
Hi,

I am using RStan and I have created a user-defined function. I need to give as input to the function a matrix of integers, so that I can then use the entries X[i,j] as indices for another matrix entry.
Is it possible to do that in Stan? When I define the input as (, ...., matrix X) it will not work because then I cannot use real numbers as indices. However, defining the input as (, ...., int[,] X) does not seem to work either :\ The latter I cannot understand why.

I am exposing the code of the function and providing the appropriate [int: , int: ] matrix as input to the function when running it afterwards in R, so I suppose that the problem is in the (, ...., int[,] X) definition of the argument in stan code.

Currently, this is the mistake that I am getting: 
VECTOR_ELT() can only be applied to a 'list', not a 'integer'

Thks in advance.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to provide matrix of integers to user-defined function
parts:
I don't know if this will help with your R issues, but
in Stan, matrices are always floating point. If you want
a 2D structure of integers, you need an array, as in:

int x[M, N];

to create an (M x N) array x of integers.

- Bob
